new_statements.quote: 5. Stress. Word-initial stress is the norm. The placement of stress is also related to the tone contour. [...] 6.2 Contour and stress [...] In the basic tone contours word-initial stress is the norm. However, in polysyllabic words, as well as in mono and disyllablic words with suffixes, a shift of the stress may take place. In words with non-falling contour, the primary stress remains on the word-initial syllable; whereas in words with falling contour the primary stress shifts, in general, from the word-initial to the word-final syllable when this contour undergoes modification.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Jirel is a word-tone language with four contrastive tone patterns (high/low register x non-falling/falling contour, register realised on the initial syllable, contour over the phonological word). Default primary stress is on the word-initial syllable. In words with the falling-contour patterns (3 and 4), when suffixation or three-plus syllables cause the falling contour to be replaced by a rising one, primary stress generally shifts to the word-final syllable; non-falling-contour words keep initial stress.
new_statements.secondary_stress: p. 861: 'In polysyllabic words with a modified tone contour both primary and secondary stress have been observed' (no placement rule given for the secondary stress).
new_statements.exceptions: Stress shift to the final syllable co-occurs with contour modification under case marking for tone pattern 4 nouns (Appendix 1, nouns, p. ~818); some nouns marked '!' retain the falling contour and do not modify; negated verbs 'generally undergo a shift of tone pattern and a shift of stress. In the past tense the main stress usually shifts to the negative marker' ma- (p. 839). p. 863 adds that without the stress shift the modified patterns 3/4 would be hard to distinguish from rising-contour patterns 1/2.
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the phonological word ('The main domain of tone is the phonological word.. Word breaks are conditioned phonologically by tone patterns'); statements cover unaffixed citation forms (initial stress) and suffixed/polysyllabic words (shift to final with contour modification). Impressionistic description by the SIL fieldworkers (fieldwork since 1970), no instrumental data.
new_statements.identity_note: The 2005 dictionary and its pronunciation guide are based on the speech of the Jirel mother-tongue compilers raised in Yarsa village, Jiri (Dolakha District); the compilers note dialect variation within Jirel is minor. Same language as Glottolog jire1238 / ISO jul; the 1973 CSDPN notes describe 'the dialect of Jiri of Dolkha District'.

sources.note: 'Word-initial stress is the norm'; stress interacts with the four word-tone patterns: with non-falling contour primary stress stays initial, with falling-contour patterns (3, 4) primary stress generally shifts to the word-final syllable when suffixation/polysyllabicity modifies the contour to rising; primary and secondary stress both observed in such words; in negated past-tense verbs main stress usually shifts to the negative prefix ma-.
